overview:
How to use this book

This companion gathers the people who matter most to the Old Testament story, from Adam to Malachi and the rulers of the nations around Israel. It is arranged in nine parts that follow the story in order. Each entry gives the person's role, approximate dates, the places and books where they appear, a short account of who they were, one key verse from the American Standard Version and passages to read.

Dates before about 1000 BC are approximate and follow the traditional chronology; many scholars date the patriarchs, the Exodus and the judges differently. Where the New Testament speaks of a person, the entry points to those passages.

parts.title: Beginnings
parts.intro: From creation to the flood, Genesis tells of the first people, the first sin and God's first promises of rescue. These chapters set the stage for the whole Bible story.

people.name: Adam and Eve
people.role: The first man and woman
facts: Genesis; also named in Luke, Romans, 1 Corinthians, 1 Timothy
paras: God formed Adam from the dust and Eve from Adam's side, and placed them in Eden to tend the garden and to walk with him. Tempted by the serpent, they ate the forbidden fruit, hid from God and were sent out of the garden, and death entered the world. Even in judgment God promised that the woman's seed would crush the serpent's head (Genesis 3:15). Paul calls Christ the last Adam, who brings life where the first Adam brought death (Romans 5:12–19; 1 Corinthians 15:22, 45).
people.quote: “And God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.”

people.name: Cain and Abel
people.role: The first brothers; the first murder
facts: Genesis; also named in Matthew, Luke, Hebrews, 1 John, Jude
paras: Adam and Eve's first sons. Abel, a shepherd, offered the firstlings of his flock and God accepted it; Cain, a farmer, brought fruit of the ground and was angry when his offering was not accepted. Cain killed his brother in the field and was sent away as a wanderer, though God put a mark on him for protection. Hebrews remembers Abel's offering as an act of faith (Hebrews 11:4), and 1 John warns believers not to be like Cain (1 John 3:12).
people.quote: “If thou doest well, shall it not be lifted up? and if thou doest not well, sin coucheth at the door; and unto thee shall be its desire; but do thou rule over it.”

people.name: Enoch
people.role: The man who walked with God
facts: Genesis; also named in Luke, Hebrews, Jude
paras: A descendant of Seth and the father of Methuselah. Genesis says twice that he walked with God, and that he was not, for God took him, without telling of his death. Hebrews names him among the heroes of faith who pleased God (Hebrews 11:5), and Jude quotes a prophecy of judgment in his name (Jude 14–15).
people.quote: “and Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.”

people.name: Noah
people.role: Builder of the ark
facts: The ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat
Genesis; also named in Isaiah, Ezekiel, Matthew, Luke, Hebrews, 1 and 2 Peter
paras: When the earth was filled with violence, Noah found favor in the eyes of Jehovah. He built the ark as God commanded and was saved through the flood with his family and the animals. Afterward God made a covenant with him and with every living creature, setting his bow in the cloud as its sign. Jesus pointed to the days of Noah as a picture of his own return (Matthew 24:37–39), and Peter calls Noah a preacher of righteousness (2 Peter 2:5).
people.quote: “But Noah found favor in the eyes of Jehovah.”

parts.title: The Patriarchs
parts.intro: God called one man and promised to bless all nations through his family. The stories of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph trace that promise through four generations.

people.name: Abraham
people.role: Father of the faithful
paras: God called Abram from Ur and Haran to a land he would show him, promising to make him a great nation and to bless all the families of the earth through him. Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness. God sealed the promise with a covenant and with circumcision, gave him Isaac in old age, and then tested him on Mount Moriah. Paul makes Abraham the model of faith for Jew and Gentile alike (Romans 4; Galatians 3).
people.quote: “And he believed in Jehovah; and he reckoned it to him for righteousness.”

people.name: Sarah
people.role: Wife of Abraham; mother of Isaac
facts: Genesis; also named in Isaiah, Romans, Galatians, Hebrews, 1 Peter
paras: Abraham's wife and half-sister, who traveled with him from Ur. Barren for many years, she gave her servant Hagar to Abraham, then laughed when God promised her a son at ninety. The Lord answered, Is anything too hard for Jehovah? and Isaac, whose name means laughter, was born. She was buried in the cave of Machpelah at Hebron. Hebrews praises her faith, and Peter holds her up as an example to wives (Hebrews 11:11; 1 Peter 3:6).
people.quote: “Is anything too hard for Jehovah? At the set time I will return unto thee, when the season cometh round, and Sarah shall have a son.”

people.name: Hagar and Ishmael
people.role: Sarah's Egyptian servant and her son
facts: Canaan; the wilderness of Beer-sheba and Paran
Genesis; also named in 1 Chronicles, Galatians
paras: Hagar, an Egyptian servant, bore Ishmael to Abraham when Sarah was barren. Twice she was driven into the wilderness, and twice God met her: she named him the God that seeth. God promised that Ishmael too would become a great nation, and he became the father of twelve princes. Paul uses Hagar and Sarah as an allegory of the old covenant of Sinai and the new covenant of promise (Galatians 4:21–31).
people.quote: “And she called the name of Jehovah that spake unto her, Thou art a God that seeth: for she said, Have I even here looked after him that seeth me?”

people.name: Lot
people.role: Abraham's nephew, rescued from Sodom
facts: Genesis; also named in Deuteronomy, Luke, 2 Peter
paras: The son of Abraham's brother Haran, who traveled with Abraham to Canaan. When their flocks grew too large, Lot chose the well-watered plain and settled in Sodom. Abraham rescued him from raiding kings and later pleaded with God for the city. Angels brought Lot out before its destruction, but his wife looked back and became a pillar of salt. Jesus told his hearers to remember Lot's wife (Luke 17:28–32).
people.quote: “But he lingered; and the men laid hold upon his hand, and upon the hand of his wife, and upon the hand of his two daughters, Jehovah being merciful unto him: and they brought him forth, and set him without the city.”

people.name: Melchizedek
people.role: King of Salem and priest of God Most High
paras: A priest-king who met Abraham after his victory over the kings, brought out bread and wine, and blessed him in the name of God Most High; Abraham gave him a tenth of everything. He appears only briefly, but Psalm 110 promises a king who is a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek. Hebrews explains that Jesus is that priest, holding a priesthood older and greater than Aaron's (Hebrews 5–7).
people.quote: “And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was priest of God Most High.”

people.name: Isaac
people.role: Son of the promise
paras: The son born to Abraham and Sarah in their old age, as God had promised. As a youth he was bound on the altar on Mount Moriah until God provided a ram in his place. He married Rebekah, a relative from Haran, and was the father of the twins Esau and Jacob. God renewed his covenant promises to him. Hebrews sees in his near-sacrifice a picture of resurrection (Hebrews 11:17–19).
people.quote: “And Abraham said, God will provide himself the lamb for a burnt-offering, my son: so they went both of them together.”

people.name: Rebekah
people.role: Wife of Isaac; mother of Esau and Jacob
paras: Abraham's servant found her at a well near Haran, where her kindness to a stranger and his camels marked her as God's choice for Isaac. She left her family at once to marry him. Before her twins were born God told her the elder would serve the younger, and later she helped Jacob deceive his blind father to receive the blessing, which drove Jacob into exile. Paul cites the word given to her as an example of God's choosing (Romans 9:10–13).
people.quote: “And they called Rebekah, and said unto her, Wilt thou go with this man? And she said, I will go.”

people.name: Esau
people.role: Isaac's elder twin; father of the Edomites
facts: Genesis; also named in Malachi, Romans, Hebrews
paras: The firstborn twin, a skilful hunter and his father's favorite. Coming in hungry from the field, he sold his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of red stew, and he later lost the blessing through Jacob's deceit. Years afterward he met his returning brother with an embrace instead of revenge. His descendants, the Edomites, became Israel's neighbors and rivals. Hebrews warns believers not to be profane like Esau, who traded what was holy for one meal (Hebrews 12:16–17).
people.quote: “And Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentils; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way: so Esau despised his birthright.”

people.name: Jacob
people.role: Father of the twelve tribes
paras: Isaac's younger twin, who took his brother's birthright and blessing and fled to Haran. On the way God met him in a dream of a ladder reaching to heaven and renewed the promise to Abraham. He served twenty years for Rachel and Leah and became the father of twelve sons. Returning home, he wrestled through the night with a mysterious man and received the new name Israel. He died in Egypt after blessing his sons, the fathers of the twelve tribes.
people.quote: “And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for thou hast striven with God and with men, and hast prevailed.”

people.name: Rachel and Leah
people.role: Wives of Jacob; mothers of Israel
facts: Haran; Canaan; Rachel buried near Bethlehem
Genesis; also named in Ruth, Jeremiah, Matthew
paras: Daughters of Laban. Jacob loved Rachel and served seven years for her, but Laban gave him Leah first. Leah, less loved, bore six sons, among them Levi and Judah, the fathers of the priests and of the royal line of David and Jesus. Rachel bore Joseph and died giving birth to Benjamin near Bethlehem. Jeremiah's picture of Rachel weeping for her children is quoted in Matthew at the killing of Bethlehem's children (Matthew 2:18).
people.quote: “And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her.”

people.name: Joseph
people.role: Dreamer, slave and ruler of Egypt
facts: Genesis; also named in Exodus, Psalms, Acts, Hebrews
paras: Jacob's favorite son, whose dreams and many-colored coat made his brothers hate him. They sold him into slavery in Egypt, where he was falsely accused and imprisoned, yet Jehovah was with him. He interpreted Pharaoh's dreams, became ruler over Egypt, and saved many from famine, including the brothers who had betrayed him. He told them, Ye meant evil against me; but God meant it for good. Stephen tells his story as part of Israel's history (Acts 7:9–16).
people.quote: “And as for you, ye meant evil against me; but God meant it for good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.”

people.name: Job
people.role: The righteous sufferer
facts: Unknown; often placed in the age of the patriarchs
Job; also named in Ezekiel and James
paras: A blameless and upright man of great wealth who lost his children, his possessions and his health, without being told of the heavenly scene behind his trials. He refused to curse God, argued with three friends who blamed him for his suffering, and longed to meet God face to face. When God answered from the whirlwind, Job humbled himself, and God restored him. James points to the patience of Job and the end the Lord brought about (James 5:11).
people.quote: “But as for me I know that my Redeemer liveth, And at last he will stand up upon the earth:”

parts.title: The Exodus and the Wilderness
parts.intro: God heard his people's cry in Egypt, brought them out through the sea, gave them his law at Sinai and led them forty years through the wilderness.

people.name: Moses
people.role: Deliverer, lawgiver and prophet
facts: About 1525–1405 BC on the early dating; others place the Exodus in the 1200s BC
Egypt, Midian, Sinai, the wilderness, Mount Nebo
Exodus to Deuteronomy; named throughout both Testaments
paras: Born a Hebrew slave and raised in Pharaoh's palace, Moses fled to Midian after killing an Egyptian. At the burning bush God revealed his name, I AM THAT I AM, and sent him back to lead Israel out of Egypt. Through the plagues, the Passover and the parting of the sea God set his people free, and at Sinai Moses received the law and the plan of the tabernacle. He led Israel forty years in the wilderness and died within sight of the promised land. Moses spoke of a prophet like himself, whom Peter identifies as Jesus (Acts 3:22).
people.quote: “And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.”

people.name: Aaron
people.role: Brother of Moses; Israel's first high priest
facts: Egypt, Sinai, the wilderness; died on Mount Hor
Exodus to Deuteronomy; also named in Psalms, Luke, Acts, Hebrews
paras: Moses' older brother, who spoke for him before Pharaoh. While Moses was on the mountain, Aaron gave in to the people and made the golden calf, yet God appointed him and his sons as priests. He wore the breastplate with the names of the twelve tribes and entered the most holy place once a year on the Day of Atonement. His rod that budded confirmed his calling. Hebrews contrasts Aaron's priesthood, carried on by men who die, with Christ's eternal priesthood (Hebrews 7:11–28).
people.quote: “Jehovah bless thee, and keep thee: Jehovah make his face to shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee: Jehovah lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace.”

people.name: Miriam
people.role: Prophetess; sister of Moses and Aaron
facts: Egypt, the Red Sea, the wilderness; died at Kadesh
Exodus, Numbers; also Deuteronomy, 1 Chronicles, Micah
paras: As a girl she watched over baby Moses in the reeds and arranged for their mother to nurse him. After the crossing of the Red Sea she took a timbrel and led the women in a song of victory. Later she and Aaron spoke against Moses, and she was struck with leprosy for seven days until Moses prayed for her. Micah remembers her with Moses and Aaron as leaders God sent before his people (Micah 6:4).
people.quote: “And Miriam answered them, Sing ye to Jehovah, for he hath triumphed gloriously; The horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.”

people.name: The Pharaoh of the Exodus
people.role: King of Egypt who resisted God
facts: About 1446 BC on the early dating, or about 1260 BC on the late dating
paras: Exodus does not give his name. He refused to let Israel go, and through ten plagues his heart was hardened as God showed his power over Egypt and its gods. After the death of the firstborn he released the people, then pursued them to the sea, where his army was drowned. Paul quotes God's word to Pharaoh, For this very purpose did I raise thee up, to show God's purpose in judgment (Romans 9:17).
people.quote: “And Pharaoh said, Who is Jehovah, that I should hearken unto his voice to let Israel go? I know not Jehovah, and moreover I will not let Israel go.”

people.name: Jethro
people.role: Priest of Midian; Moses' father-in-law
paras: The priest of Midian who welcomed Moses when he fled Egypt and gave him his daughter Zipporah as wife. Moses kept Jethro's flocks for forty years before the burning bush. After the Exodus Jethro came to Moses in the wilderness, rejoiced at all God had done, and offered sacrifices. He advised Moses to share the work of judging with able men, which shaped Israel's leadership.
people.quote: “Now I know that Jehovah is greater than all gods; yea, in the thing wherein they dealt proudly against them.”

people.name: Caleb
people.role: Faithful spy who followed God fully
paras: One of the twelve spies sent into Canaan. Ten brought back a fearful report, but Caleb and Joshua urged the people to trust God and go up at once. Because he wholly followed Jehovah, God promised that he would enter the land. Forty-five years later, at eighty-five, he asked for the hill country of Hebron, still held by giants, and took it.
people.quote: “but my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land whereinto he went; and his seed shall possess it.”

people.name: Balaam
people.role: Diviner hired to curse Israel
facts: Pethor on the Euphrates; the plains of Moab
Numbers; also Deuteronomy, Joshua, Micah, 2 Peter, Jude, Revelation
paras: A famous diviner whom Balak king of Moab hired to curse Israel. On the way his donkey saw the angel of Jehovah blocking the road and spoke to him. Each time Balaam opened his mouth, God turned the curse into a blessing, including a prophecy of a star out of Jacob. Afterward he advised Moab to lead Israel into idolatry. The New Testament makes him a warning against greed and false teaching (2 Peter 2:15; Revelation 2:14).
people.quote: “I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not nigh: There shall come forth a star out of Jacob, And a sceptre shall rise out of Israel, And shall smite through the corners of Moab, And break down all the sons of tumult.”

parts.title: The Conquest and the Judges
parts.intro: Israel entered the land under Joshua, then lived through cycles of turning away, oppression and rescue, when every man did that which was right in his own eyes.

people.name: Joshua
people.role: Moses' successor; leader of the conquest
facts: About 1406–1375 BC for the conquest (early dating)
The wilderness, Jericho, Ai, Shiloh, Shechem
Exodus to Joshua; also Judges, 1 Kings, Acts, Hebrews
paras: Moses' assistant, who led Israel's army against Amalek and was one of the two faithful spies. After Moses died, God commanded him to be strong and of good courage and led Israel across the Jordan on dry ground. The walls of Jericho fell, and Joshua divided the land among the tribes. At the end of his life he challenged the people at Shechem to choose whom they would serve. His Hebrew name is the same as the name Jesus.
people.quote: “And if it seem evil unto you to serve Jehovah, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve Jehovah.”

people.name: Rahab
people.role: Woman of Jericho who sheltered the spies
paras: A harlot of Jericho who hid Joshua's two spies and let them down by a scarlet cord from her window, confessing that Jehovah is God in heaven above and on earth beneath. When the city fell, she and her family were spared. She married into Israel and became an ancestor of David and of Jesus (Matthew 1:5). Hebrews and James both name her as an example of faith shown in action.
people.quote: “And as soon as we had heard it, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more spirit in any man, because of you: for Jehovah your God, he is God in heaven above, and on earth beneath.”

people.name: Deborah
people.role: Prophetess and judge
facts: About 1200s BC (dates in the period of the judges are uncertain)
Between Ramah and Bethel; Mount Tabor; the river Kishon
paras: A prophetess who judged Israel under a palm tree in the hill country of Ephraim. When Jabin king of Canaan oppressed Israel, she summoned Barak to lead ten thousand men against his commander Sisera, whose iron chariots were swept away by the river Kishon. Sisera fled and was killed by Jael. Deborah and Barak's song of victory is one of the oldest poems in the Bible.
people.quote: “And Deborah said unto Barak, Up; for this is the day in which Jehovah hath delivered Sisera into thy hand; is not Jehovah gone out before thee? So Barak went down from mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.”

people.name: Gideon
people.role: Judge who defeated Midian with three hundred men
facts: Ophrah in Manasseh; the valley of Jezreel
paras: The angel of Jehovah found him threshing wheat in hiding from the Midianites and called him a mighty man of valor. He tore down his father's altar to Baal, asked for signs with a fleece, and saw God reduce his army from thirty-two thousand to three hundred. With trumpets, pitchers and torches they routed Midian at night. He refused to be king, saying Jehovah shall rule over you, but his later ephod became a snare to Israel.
people.quote: “And Jehovah said unto Gideon, By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you, and deliver the Midianites into thy hand; and let all the people go every man unto his place.”

people.name: Samson
people.role: Nazirite judge of great strength
paras: His birth was announced by an angel, and he was set apart as a Nazirite from the womb. The Spirit of Jehovah gave him great strength against the Philistines: he tore apart a lion and struck down a thousand men with a jawbone. But he was ruled by his desires, and Delilah betrayed the secret of his uncut hair. Blinded and imprisoned, he prayed for strength one last time and pulled down the temple of Dagon on the Philistine lords.
people.quote: “And Samson called unto Jehovah, and said, O Lord Jehovah, remember me, I pray thee, and strengthen me, I pray thee, only this once, O God, that I may be at once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes.”

people.name: Ruth and Naomi
people.role: A Moabite daughter-in-law and her mother-in-law
facts: In the days of the judges, about 1100 BC
Ruth; Ruth also named in Matthew
paras: Naomi of Bethlehem lost her husband and both sons in Moab and returned home bitter and empty. Her widowed daughter-in-law Ruth refused to leave her, pledging herself to Naomi's people and Naomi's God. Gleaning in the fields of Boaz, Ruth found kindness, and Naomi guided her to seek Boaz as kinsman-redeemer. Their son Obed was the grandfather of David, and Ruth is named in Jesus' genealogy (Matthew 1:5).
people.quote: “And Ruth said, Entreat me not to leave thee, and to return from following after thee, for whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge; thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God;”

people.name: Boaz
people.role: Kinsman-redeemer of Bethlehem
facts: Ruth; also named in 1 Chronicles, Matthew, Luke
paras: A wealthy landowner of Bethlehem and a relative of Naomi's husband. He welcomed the foreigner Ruth to glean in his fields and protected her. When she asked him to act as kinsman-redeemer, he went to the city gate, redeemed the family land and married her. Their great-grandson was King David, and Boaz is named in the genealogies of Jesus (Matthew 1:5; Luke 3:32).
people.quote: “Jehovah recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of Jehovah, the God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to take refuge.”

parts.title: The United Kingdom
parts.intro: Israel asked for a king. Under Saul, David and Solomon the tribes became one nation with Jerusalem as its capital and the temple at its heart.

people.name: Hannah
people.role: Mother of Samuel; woman of prayer
paras: Childless and taunted by her husband's other wife, Hannah poured out her soul before Jehovah at the tabernacle in Shiloh and vowed to give him her son. Eli the priest thought she was drunk, then blessed her. When Samuel was weaned, she brought him to serve at Shiloh. Her song of praise, The bow of the mighty men are broken, is echoed in Mary's Magnificat (Luke 1:46–55).
people.quote: “For this child I prayed; and Jehovah hath given me my petition which I asked of him:”

people.name: Eli
people.role: Priest and judge at Shiloh
paras: The aged high priest at Shiloh who raised young Samuel. When the boy heard a voice in the night, Eli taught him to answer, Speak; for thy servant heareth. But Eli failed to restrain his wicked sons Hophni and Phinehas, and God warned that his house would be judged. When news came that the ark had been captured by the Philistines and his sons killed, Eli fell backward and died.
people.quote: “Therefore Eli said unto Samuel, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, Jehovah; for thy servant heareth. So Samuel went and lay down in his place.”

people.name: Samuel
people.role: Prophet, priest and last of the judges
facts: 1 Samuel; also 1 Chronicles, Psalms, Jeremiah, Acts, Hebrews
paras: Given to God by his mother Hannah, Samuel grew up at Shiloh and was called by God as a boy. He judged Israel and led them to repentance at Mizpah. When the people demanded a king, he warned them of the cost and then anointed Saul, and later, when Saul disobeyed, he anointed the young shepherd David. Samuel told Saul that to obey is better than sacrifice.
people.quote: “And Samuel said, Hath Jehovah as great delight in burnt-offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of Jehovah? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.”

people.name: Saul
people.role: Israel's first king
paras: A tall, impressive man of the tribe of Benjamin, anointed by Samuel as the first king. He began with victories but offered a sacrifice he had no right to make and spared what God had commanded him to destroy, so God rejected him as king. Tormented and jealous, he hunted David for years. He consulted a medium at En-dor before his last battle and died with his sons on Mount Gilboa.
people.quote: “For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as idolatry and teraphim. Because thou hast rejected the word of Jehovah, he hath also rejected thee from being king.”

people.name: Jonathan
people.role: Son of Saul; David's loyal friend
paras: Saul's eldest son and heir, a brave warrior who with his armor-bearer attacked a Philistine garrison, trusting that nothing restrains Jehovah to save by many or by few. After David killed Goliath, Jonathan loved him as his own soul and made a covenant with him, giving him his robe and sword. He warned David of Saul's plans and recognized that David would be king. He died with his father at Gilboa, and David mourned him in a famous lament.
people.quote: “And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.”

people.name: Goliath
people.role: Philistine champion of Gath
paras: A giant warrior from Gath who defied the armies of Israel for forty days. While Saul's soldiers trembled, the young shepherd David came with a sling and five smooth stones, declaring that the battle is Jehovah's. A single stone struck Goliath in the forehead, and David took his sword. The story became a lasting picture of God's power working through the weak.
people.quote: “Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a javelin: but I come to thee in the name of Jehovah of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.”

people.name: David
people.role: Shepherd, king and psalmist
facts: Born about 1040 BC; reigned about 1010–970 BC
Bethlehem, the wilderness of Judah, Hebron, Jerusalem
1 Samuel to 1 Kings, 1 Chronicles, Psalms; named throughout both Testaments
paras: The youngest son of Jesse of Bethlehem, anointed by Samuel while still a shepherd. He killed Goliath, served Saul and then fled from him, and became king first at Hebron and then over all Israel, making Jerusalem his capital. God promised that his throne would be established for ever. He sinned grievously with Bathsheba and against Uriah, repented when Nathan confronted him, and suffered sorrow in his own house. A man after God's own heart, he wrote many of the psalms, and Jesus is called the son of David.
people.quote: “And thy house and thy kingdom shall be made sure for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever.”

people.name: Bathsheba
people.role: Wife of Uriah, then of David; mother of Solomon
facts: 2 Samuel, 1 Kings; also 1 Chronicles, Psalm 51 (title), Matthew
paras: The wife of Uriah the Hittite, one of David's loyal soldiers. David saw her from his roof, took her, and when she conceived had Uriah killed in battle. Their first child died, but she later bore Solomon. In David's old age she and Nathan secured Solomon's succession to the throne. Matthew includes her, as the wife of Uriah, in the genealogy of Jesus (Matthew 1:6).
people.quote: “verily as I sware unto thee by Jehovah, the God of Israel, saying, Assuredly Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne in my stead; verily so will I do this day.”

people.name: Nathan
people.role: Prophet to King David
facts: 2 Samuel, 1 Kings; also 1 and 2 Chronicles, Psalm 51 (title)
paras: The prophet who brought David God's promise of an everlasting house and kingdom. After David's sin with Bathsheba, Nathan told him a parable of a rich man who stole a poor man's only lamb, and when David burned with anger, Nathan said, Thou art the man. David confessed, and Psalm 51 is linked with that moment. Nathan later helped ensure that Solomon became king.
people.quote: “And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;”

people.name: Absalom
people.role: David's son who rebelled against him
facts: Jerusalem; Hebron; the forest of Ephraim
paras: David's handsome third son. After avenging his sister Tamar by killing his brother Amnon, he fled and was later restored, but he stole the hearts of the people and proclaimed himself king at Hebron. David fled Jerusalem. In the battle in the forest of Ephraim, Absalom's long hair caught in an oak and Joab killed him. David's grief, O my son Absalom, is among the most moving laments in Scripture.
people.quote: “And the king was much moved, and went up to the chamber over the gate, and wept: and as he went, thus he said, O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would I had died for thee, O Absalom, my son, my son!”

people.name: Solomon
people.role: King of Israel; builder of the temple
facts: 1 Kings, 2 Chronicles, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, Song of Solomon; also Matthew, Luke, Acts
paras: David and Bathsheba's son, who asked God for an understanding heart to judge the people and was given wisdom, riches and honor. He built the temple in Jerusalem and dedicated it with a great prayer, and his fame drew the queen of Sheba. Proverbs, Ecclesiastes and the Song of Solomon are linked with his name. But his many foreign wives turned his heart to other gods, and after his death the kingdom divided. Jesus said one greater than Solomon was here (Matthew 12:42).
people.quote: “Give thy servant therefore an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and evil; for who is able to judge this thy great people?”

parts.title: The Divided Kingdom
parts.intro: After Solomon the kingdom split: Israel in the north with Samaria as its capital, and Judah in the south with Jerusalem. Assyria destroyed Israel in 722 BC, and Babylon took Judah in 586 BC.

people.name: Rehoboam
people.role: Solomon's son; first king of Judah
facts: 1 Kings, 2 Chronicles; also named in Matthew
paras: When the people asked Solomon's son to lighten their heavy burdens, he rejected the counsel of the old men and followed his young friends: My father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions. The ten northern tribes broke away under Jeroboam, leaving him only Judah and Benjamin. During his reign Shishak of Egypt invaded and carried off the temple treasures.
people.quote: “and spake to them after the counsel of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to your yoke: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.”

people.name: Jeroboam
people.role: First king of the northern kingdom of Israel
paras: An official of Solomon to whom the prophet Ahijah promised ten of the twelve tribes. After the kingdom split, Jeroboam feared his people would return to Jerusalem to worship, so he set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan and appointed his own priests. Kings of Israel are judged again and again as walking in the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, wherewith he made Israel to sin.
people.quote: “Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold; and he said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.”

people.name: Ahab
people.role: King of Israel who served Baal
paras: The son of Omri, who did evil in the sight of Jehovah above all that were before him. He married Jezebel of Sidon and built a temple to Baal in Samaria. Elijah announced a drought and confronted Baal's prophets on Mount Carmel during his reign. After Jezebel had Naboth killed for his vineyard, Elijah pronounced judgment on Ahab. He died from a random arrow at Ramoth-gilead, as the prophet Micaiah had foretold.
people.quote: “And it came to pass, when Ahab saw Elijah, that Ahab said unto him, Is it thou, thou troubler of Israel?”

people.name: Jezebel
people.role: Queen of Israel; promoter of Baal worship
facts: 1 and 2 Kings; her name is used in Revelation
paras: A princess of Sidon who married Ahab and championed the worship of Baal, killing the prophets of Jehovah and threatening Elijah's life after Carmel. She arranged false witnesses to have Naboth stoned so Ahab could take his vineyard. Years later, at Jehu's command, she was thrown from a window in Jezreel, as Elijah had foretold. In Revelation her name stands for a false prophetess leading believers astray (Revelation 2:20).
people.quote: “(But there was none like unto Ahab, who did sell himself to do that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah, whom Jezebel his wife stirred up.”

people.name: Jehoshaphat
people.role: King of Judah who sought God
paras: A good king of Judah who removed idols and sent officials and Levites to teach the law throughout the land. When a great army of Moab and Ammon came against him, he proclaimed a fast and prayed, We know not what to do, but our eyes are upon thee. He sent singers before the army, and the enemies destroyed one another. His alliance with Ahab's house, however, brought trouble on Judah.
people.quote: “O our God, wilt thou not judge them? for we have no might against this great company that cometh against us; neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee.”

people.name: Jehu
people.role: King of Israel who wiped out Ahab's house
paras: An army commander anointed by a messenger of Elisha to destroy the house of Ahab, as Elijah had foretold. He drove furiously to Jezreel, killed King Joram and Jezebel, and then gathered the worshipers of Baal into their temple and destroyed them. Yet he kept Jeroboam's golden calves. His bloodshed went beyond what God approved, and Hosea later announced judgment for the blood of Jezreel (Hosea 1:4).
people.quote: “And the watchman told, saying, He came even unto them, and cometh not back: and the driving is like the driving of Jehu the son of Nimshi; for he driveth furiously.”

people.name: Hezekiah
people.role: King of Judah who trusted God against Assyria
facts: 2 Kings, 2 Chronicles, Isaiah; also Proverbs, Jeremiah, Matthew
paras: One of Judah's best kings, who reopened and cleansed the temple, celebrated a great Passover, and broke the bronze serpent that had become an idol. When Sennacherib of Assyria besieged Jerusalem, Hezekiah spread the enemy's letter before Jehovah and prayed, and the angel of Jehovah struck the Assyrian camp. When he was sick to death, God added fifteen years to his life. His pride in showing his treasures to Babylon's envoys drew Isaiah's warning of exile.
people.quote: “He trusted in Jehovah, the God of Israel; so that after him was none like him among all the kings of Judah, nor among them that were before him.”

people.name: Manasseh
people.role: Judah's most wicked king, who repented
paras: Hezekiah's son, who undid his father's reforms: he rebuilt altars to Baal, placed idols in the temple, practised sorcery and made his son pass through the fire, and shed much innocent blood. 2 Kings names his sins as a cause of Judah's exile. Yet 2 Chronicles records that when the Assyrians took him captive to Babylon he humbled himself greatly, and God heard him and brought him back to Jerusalem.
people.quote: “And he prayed unto him; and he was entreated of him, and heard his supplication, and brought him again to Jerusalem into his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that Jehovah he was God.”

people.name: Josiah
people.role: Boy king of Judah who renewed the covenant
facts: 2 Kings, 2 Chronicles; also Jeremiah, Zephaniah, Matthew
paras: Made king at eight years old after his father's murder. While the temple was being repaired, the high priest found the book of the law. When Josiah heard its words he tore his clothes, sought God through the prophetess Huldah, and led the people in renewing the covenant. He destroyed idols throughout the land, even the altar at Bethel, as a prophet had foretold three centuries earlier, and kept a great Passover. He died in battle against Pharaoh Neco at Megiddo.
people.quote: “And like unto him was there no king before him, that turned to Jehovah with all his heart, and with all his soul, and with all his might, according to all the law of Moses; neither after him arose there any like him.”

people.name: Zedekiah
people.role: Last king of Judah
paras: Placed on the throne by Nebuchadnezzar, he rebelled against Babylon despite Jeremiah's repeated warnings to submit. He consulted the prophet secretly but would not obey him and let his officials throw Jeremiah into a cistern. When Jerusalem fell in 586 BC, Zedekiah fled but was captured; he saw his sons killed, then was blinded and taken in chains to Babylon. The temple was burned and the people carried into exile.
people.quote: “Then said Jeremiah unto Zedekiah, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of hosts, the God of Israel: If thou wilt go forth unto the king of Babylon’s princes, then thy soul shall live, and this city shall not be burned with fire; and thou shalt live, and thy house.”

parts.title: The Prophets
parts.intro: God sent prophets to call his people back to the covenant, to warn of judgment and to promise a coming King and a new covenant.

people.name: Elijah
people.role: Prophet of fire who confronted Baal
facts: Gilead, the brook Cherith, Zarephath, Mount Carmel, Horeb, the Jordan
1 and 2 Kings; also Malachi and the Gospels, Romans, James
paras: A prophet from Gilead who announced a drought to King Ahab and was fed by ravens and by a widow of Zarephath, whose son he raised. On Mount Carmel he challenged the prophets of Baal, and God answered by fire. Fleeing Jezebel, he met God at Horeb in a still small voice. He was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind with chariots of fire. Malachi promised his return before the day of Jehovah; Jesus said John the Baptist came in that spirit, and Elijah appeared at the Transfiguration.
people.quote: “And Elijah came near unto all the people, and said, How long go ye limping between the two sides? if Jehovah be God, follow him; but if Baal, then follow him. And the people answered him not a word.”

people.name: Elisha
people.role: Elijah's successor; prophet of many miracles
facts: 1 and 2 Kings; also named in Luke
paras: Elijah threw his mantle on Elisha while he was plowing, and he left everything to follow him. When Elijah was taken up, Elisha received a double portion of his spirit. His ministry was full of miracles: healed water, multiplied oil, a Shunammite's son raised, poisoned stew made wholesome, a hundred men fed, and Naaman the Syrian healed of leprosy. Jesus pointed to Naaman's healing as God's mercy to a foreigner (Luke 4:27).
people.quote: “And he answered, Fear not; for they that are with us are more than they that are with them.”

people.name: Jonah
people.role: Reluctant prophet sent to Nineveh
paras: A prophet from Galilee who foretold Jeroboam II's victories. Sent to preach against Nineveh, Assyria's great city, he fled by ship toward Tarshish, was thrown overboard in a storm, and was swallowed by a great fish for three days and nights. When he finally preached, Nineveh repented and God spared it, to Jonah's anger. God's closing question shows his compassion for all people. Jesus called his own death and resurrection the sign of Jonah (Matthew 12:39–41).
people.quote: “But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that which I have vowed. Salvation is of Jehovah.”

people.name: Amos
people.role: Shepherd prophet of justice
facts: Tekoa in Judah; Bethel in Israel
paras: A herdsman and dresser of sycamore figs from Tekoa, who was sent to the prosperous northern kingdom under Jeroboam II. He condemned the rich who trampled the poor and turned worship into empty ritual, and called for justice to roll down as waters. The priest at Bethel told him to go home. His closing promise that God would raise up the fallen tabernacle of David is quoted at the Jerusalem council (Acts 15:16–17).
people.quote: “But let justice roll down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.”

people.name: Hosea
people.role: Prophet whose marriage pictured God's love
facts: Hosea; also quoted in Matthew, Romans, 1 Peter
paras: God told Hosea to marry Gomer, who proved unfaithful, so that his own heartbreak would picture Israel's unfaithfulness to God. He named his children with messages of judgment, then bought Gomer back and restored her. His book speaks of God's steadfast love for a wayward people. Matthew quotes Out of Egypt did I call my son (Hosea 11:1), and Jesus twice quoted I desire goodness, and not sacrifice (Matthew 9:13; 12:7).
people.quote: “For I desire goodness, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt-offerings.”

people.name: Isaiah
people.role: Prophet of the Holy One and the Servant
facts: Isaiah, 2 Kings, 2 Chronicles; quoted throughout the New Testament
paras: A prophet in Jerusalem through the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah. In the year King Uzziah died he saw the Lord high and lifted up, cried Woe is me, and answered Here am I; send me. He counselled Ahaz and Hezekiah, foretold Assyria's defeat at Jerusalem, and spoke of the virgin's son Immanuel, the child whose name is Wonderful, Counsellor, and the suffering Servant wounded for our transgressions. The New Testament quotes him more than any other prophet.
people.quote: “But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities; the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.”

people.name: Micah
people.role: Prophet who foretold Bethlehem
paras: A prophet from the countryside of Judah, a contemporary of Isaiah, who spoke against corrupt rulers, priests and prophets in both Samaria and Jerusalem. He warned that Zion would be plowed as a field, and a century later his words saved Jeremiah's life (Jeremiah 26:18–19). He foretold that a ruler would come from little Bethlehem, which the scribes quoted to Herod (Matthew 2:5–6), and summed up God's requirements: to do justly, love kindness, and walk humbly with God.
people.quote: “He hath showed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth Jehovah require of thee, but to do justly, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with thy God?”

people.name: Jeremiah
people.role: The weeping prophet of Judah's fall
facts: Jeremiah, Lamentations (by tradition), 2 Chronicles; also Daniel, Matthew, Hebrews
paras: Called as a young man from a priestly family, Jeremiah warned Judah for forty years that Babylon would come as God's judgment. He was beaten, imprisoned, thrown into a cistern and branded a traitor, and he poured out his grief in his laments. He saw Jerusalem fall in 586 BC and was later taken to Egypt against his will. In the darkest time he promised a new covenant, with God's law written on the heart, which Hebrews quotes in full (Hebrews 8:8–12).
people.quote: “But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith Jehovah: I will put my law in their inward parts, and in their heart will I write it; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.”

people.name: Ezekiel
people.role: Priest and prophet among the exiles
paras: A priest taken to Babylon with King Jehoiachin in 597 BC. By the river Chebar he saw a vision of God's glory on a throne of living creatures and wheels. He acted out signs of Jerusalem's siege and saw God's glory leave the temple. After the city fell he spoke of hope: a shepherd from David's line, a new heart and a new spirit, a valley of dry bones brought to life, and a new temple from which a river of life flows.
people.quote: “A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you; and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh.”

people.name: Daniel
people.role: Faithful exile and seer in Babylon
paras: Taken to Babylon as a youth in 605 BC, Daniel refused the king's food and kept faithful to God while serving in the royal court. He interpreted Nebuchadnezzar's dreams and the handwriting on the wall at Belshazzar's feast. Under Darius he kept praying toward Jerusalem despite a royal ban and was delivered from the lions' den. His visions of four kingdoms and of one like a son of man given an everlasting kingdom shaped Jesus' own title, the Son of man.
people.quote: “And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.”

parts.title: Exile and Return
parts.intro: In Babylon and Persia God preserved his people. Under Cyrus they returned to rebuild the temple and, later, the walls of Jerusalem.

people.name: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego
people.role: Daniel's friends in the fiery furnace
facts: Daniel; also alluded to in Hebrews
paras: Three young men of Judah taken to Babylon with Daniel and given Babylonian names. When Nebuchadnezzar set up a golden image and commanded all to bow, they refused, saying their God was able to deliver them, but if not, they still would not serve his gods. Thrown into a furnace heated seven times hotter, they walked unharmed with a fourth figure like a son of the gods. Hebrews remembers those who quenched the power of fire (Hebrews 11:34).
people.quote: “If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace; and he will deliver us out of thy hand, O king.”

people.name: Zerubbabel
people.role: Governor who led the return and rebuilt the temple
facts: Ezra, Nehemiah, Haggai, Zechariah; also Matthew, Luke
paras: A descendant of King David who led the first group of exiles home after Cyrus's decree in 538 BC, together with Joshua the high priest. They rebuilt the altar and laid the foundation of the temple, but opposition stopped the work for years. Encouraged by Haggai and Zechariah, Zerubbabel finished the temple in 515 BC. Zechariah's word to him was, Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit. He appears in both genealogies of Jesus.
people.quote: “Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of Jehovah unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit, saith Jehovah of hosts.”

people.name: Haggai and Zechariah
people.role: Prophets of the rebuilt temple
facts: Haggai, Zechariah, Ezra; Zechariah quoted throughout the Gospels and Revelation
paras: Two prophets who stirred the returned exiles to finish rebuilding the temple. Haggai rebuked the people for living in paneled houses while God's house lay in ruins, and promised that the latter glory of this house would be greater than the former. Zechariah's night visions encouraged Zerubbabel and Joshua, and his later chapters foretell a king coming lowly and riding upon an ass (Matthew 21:5), thirty pieces of silver, and the one whom they have pierced (John 19:37).
people.quote: “Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy king cometh unto thee; he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, even upon a colt the foal of an ass.”

people.name: Esther
people.role: Jewish queen of Persia who saved her people
paras: A Jewish orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai, who became queen to King Ahasuerus (Xerxes). When Haman plotted to destroy all the Jews in the empire, Mordecai urged her that she may have come to the kingdom for such a time as this. After three days of fasting she went to the king uninvited, saying, If I perish, I perish, and exposed Haman's plot. The feast of Purim celebrates the deliverance. God is never named in the book, yet his care runs through every turn.
people.quote: “For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, then will relief and deliverance arise to the Jews from another place, but thou and thy father’s house will perish: and who knoweth whether thou art not come to the kingdom for such a time as this?”

people.name: Mordecai
people.role: Esther's cousin; second to the king
paras: A Benjamite in exile who raised his orphaned cousin Esther. He uncovered a plot against King Ahasuerus, and his refusal to bow to Haman provoked Haman's plan to destroy the Jews. He urged Esther to act, and when the plot was overturned, Haman was hanged on the gallows he had built for Mordecai. Mordecai became second in the kingdom, seeking the good of his people.
people.quote: “For Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the good of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed.”

people.name: Ezra
people.role: Priest and scribe of the law
paras: A priest descended from Aaron and a scribe skilled in the law of Moses, who led a second group of exiles to Jerusalem in 458 BC with the backing of King Artaxerxes. He had set his heart to seek the law, to do it, and to teach it. He led the people in repentance over marriages that drew them away from God, and later, with Nehemiah, read the law publicly from morning until midday while the Levites explained its sense.
people.quote: “For Ezra had set his heart to seek the law of Jehovah, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and ordinances.”

people.name: Nehemiah
people.role: Cupbearer who rebuilt Jerusalem's walls
paras: Cupbearer to King Artaxerxes in Susa. When he heard that Jerusalem's walls lay in ruins he wept, fasted and prayed, then asked the king for leave to rebuild them. Despite mockery, threats and plots, the people built with a tool in one hand and a weapon in the other, and finished the wall in fifty-two days. He worked with Ezra to renew the covenant and reformed the people's keeping of the Sabbath and care for the temple.
people.quote: “Then answered I them, and said unto them, The God of heaven, he will prosper us; therefore we his servants will arise and build: but ye have no portion, nor right, nor memorial, in Jerusalem.”

people.name: Malachi
people.role: Last of the Old Testament prophets
facts: Malachi; quoted in the Gospels and Romans
paras: A prophet of the period after the temple was rebuilt, when worship had grown careless: priests offered blemished sacrifices, people withheld tithes and husbands dealt treacherously with their wives. Malachi answered their complaints with God's love and faithfulness. He foretold a messenger to prepare the Lord's way and the coming of Elijah before the great day of Jehovah, words the Gospels apply to John the Baptist (Mark 1:2; Matthew 11:10–14).
people.quote: “Behold, I send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the Lord, whom ye seek, will suddenly come to his temple; and the messenger of the covenant, whom ye desire, behold, he cometh, saith Jehovah of hosts.”

parts.title: Rulers of the Nations
parts.intro: The great empires that surrounded Israel appear as instruments in God's hand, raised up to discipline his people and to restore them.

people.name: Sennacherib
people.role: King of Assyria who besieged Jerusalem
facts: Ruled 705–681 BC; invaded Judah in 701 BC
paras: The Assyrian king who captured the fortified cities of Judah, including Lachish, and sent his officer to mock Hezekiah and the God of Israel outside Jerusalem's walls. In answer to Hezekiah's prayer, the angel of Jehovah struck down the Assyrian camp in one night, and Sennacherib returned to Nineveh, where he was later killed by two of his sons. His own inscriptions boast that he shut Hezekiah up like a bird in a cage, but they do not claim the city was taken.
people.quote: “And it came to pass that night, that the angel of Jehovah went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred fourscore and five thousand: and when men arose early in the morning, behold, these were all dead bodies.”

people.name: Nebuchadnezzar
people.role: King of Babylon who took Jerusalem
facts: 2 Kings, 2 Chronicles, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Daniel, Ezra
paras: The greatest king of the Babylonian empire, who took captives from Jerusalem in 605 and 597 BC and destroyed the city and temple in 586 BC. In Daniel he dreams of a great image, sets up a golden statue, and is humbled by seven years of madness until he lifts his eyes to heaven and praises the Most High. Jeremiah calls him God's servant, the instrument of judgment on Judah.
people.quote: “Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and extol and honor the King of heaven; for all his works are truth, and his ways justice; and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.”

people.name: Ahasuerus
people.role: King of Persia in the book of Esther
paras: The Persian king whose empire stretched from India to Ethiopia. He deposed Queen Vashti, chose Esther as queen, and was persuaded by Haman to issue a decree against the Jews. When Esther revealed her identity and Haman's plot, the king had Haman hanged and allowed the Jews to defend themselves. Greek historians remember him for his invasion of Greece in 480 BC.
people.quote: “Then said the king unto her, What wilt thou, queen Esther? and what is thy request? it shall be given thee even to the half of the kingdom.”

people.name: Cyrus
people.role: King of Persia who let the exiles go home
facts: Ruled 559–530 BC; conquered Babylon in 539 BC
paras: The founder of the Persian empire, who took Babylon in 539 BC and the next year decreed that the Jews could return home and rebuild the house of God in Jerusalem, returning the temple vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken. Isaiah names him as God's shepherd and anointed one, raised up for the sake of his servant Jacob. Archaeologists have found the Cyrus Cylinder, which records his policy of returning captive peoples to their lands.
people.quote: “Thus saith Cyrus king of Persia, All the kingdoms of the earth hath Jehovah, the God of heaven, given me; and he hath charged me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.”
